label: lem:zero_deriv_constant
title: Zero derivative implies constant
statement: Let $G$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ with $G'(x) = 0$ for all $x \in (a,b)$. Then $G$ is constant on $[a,b]$: we have $G(x) = G(a)$ for all $x \in [a,b]$.
proof: For any $x \in (a,b]$, the Mean Value Theorem (Lemma~\ref{lem:mvt}) applied to $[a,x]$ produces $c$ with $0 = G'(c) = \frac{G(x) - G(a)}{x - a}$, whence $G(x) = G(a)$.
